replacement_dyads.title: Pastoral Care & Piety vs. Secular Mindfulness & Coaching
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Demonstrates how confessional pastoral care (Seelsorge, Frömmigkeit) was progressively overtaken by secularized mindfulness and coaching (Achtsamkeit, Selbsthilfe) around the 2000s–2010s inflection point.
replacement_dyads.pole_a_label: RQ₁ Pastoral Care (seelsorge · gebet · frömmigkeit · predigt)

replacement_dyads.title: Divine Grace & Salvation vs. Therapeutic Healing & Resilience
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Tracks the soteriological shift from transcendent salvation and sacramental grace (Gnade, Erlösung) toward immanent psychosomatic healing and crisis resilience (Heilung, Resilienz, Wohlbefinden).

replacement_dyads.title: Institutional Church & Liturgy vs. Holistic Individual Spirituality
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Captures the de-institutionalization of German religious publishing: institutional markers (Liturgie, Pfarrer, Ökumene) contract relative to post-confessional spirituality (Spiritualität, Bewusstsein, Energie).
replacement_dyads.pole_b_label: RQ₂ Holistic Spirit (spiritualität · bewusstsein · energie · harmonie)

replacement_dyads.title: Christian Humility & Vocation vs. Neoliberal Self-Optimization
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Illustrates the replacement of self-transcending Christian ethics (Schöpfung, Evangelium, Heilig) by neoliberal performance and affective self-management (Erfolg, Glück, Selbstliebe, Motivation).

replacement_dyads.title: Confessional Dogmatics vs. Sociology of Secularization & Critique
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Quantifies the academic shift from internal dogmatic theology (Bibel, Christus, Evangelium) toward externalist sociology of religion and ideology critique (Säkularisierung, Kritik, Ideologie, Diskurs).
replacement_dyads.pole_b_label: RQ₃ Secular Critique (säkularisierung · kritik · ideologie · diskurs)

replacement_dyads.title: Clerical Hierarchy vs. Democratic Pluralism & Human Rights
replacement_dyads.thesis_claim: Shows how hierarchical ecclesiastical signifiers (Papst, Bischof, Katholisch, Evangelisch) are increasingly contextualized within constitutional democracy, pluralism, and human rights.
replacement_dyads.pole_b_label: RQ₃ Pluralist State (demokratie · pluralismus · menschenrechte · autonomie)
